title: Our Sins, Alas, How Strong They Be
description: Our Sins, Alas, How Strong They Be in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 86, headed “Freedom from sin and misery in heaven”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our sins, a-las, how strong they be! And like a vi-olent sea They break our du-ty, Lord, to thee, And hur-ry us a-way.

lines: Our sins, alas, how strong they be!
They break our duty, Lord, to thee,
The waves of trouble how they rise!
But death shall land our weary souls
There to fulfil his sweet commands
No sin shall clog our winged zeal,
There shall we sit, and sing, and tell
Till heavenly raptures fire our hearts,
For ever his dear sacred Name

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
